text: Rifampin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4.
Rifampin is a first-line antimycobacterial agent.
Rifampin colours urine and tears orange.
Rifampin is also a P-glycoprotein inducer.
Rifampin is given as part of combination therapy to limit resistance.
Ethinylestradiol is the oestrogen component of combined oral contraceptives.
Ethinylestradiol increases hepatic synthesis of clotting factors.
Ethinylestradiol is administered orally once daily in most regimens.

Yes. Rifampin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 (and of P-glycoprotein). Ethinylestradiol is extensively cleared by CYP3A4-mediated metabolism (and is a P-gp substrate), so co-administration with rifampin markedly increases its metabolic clearance and lowers plasma ethinylestradiol concentrations. This reduces contraceptive efficacy and commonly causes breakthrough bleeding or unintended pregnancy — a well-recognized, clinically significant interaction; alternative or additional non-hormonal contraception is advised. Caveat: the provided monograph covers only rifampin; this conclusion relies on the established fact that ethinylestradiol is a CYP3A4 substrate, which is not stated in the information given.

MECHANISM: CYP3A4 induction by rifampin → increased metabolism and reduced exposure of ethinylestradiol (P-gp induction may contribute)
FINAL ANSWER: YES
